newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper aims to take out resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper aims to take out resistance.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices could take out resistance at $2,404 on Friday opening the way to test more established resistances around $2,420, technical analysts said.
The recent high at $2,440 could be passed if the first two resistances are breached, they said.
COPPER
Buoyed by a surging zinc market on Thursday, copper could be poised to pass $2,400 and if that triggers buy stops, take out several significant resistance areas above that level, analysts said.
The first stop would be $2,404 last seen in mid April and if that was taken, then $2,440, the high on March 7, would be the next target, they said.
Thursday's late London close at $2,385/$2,388 was very positive for the market as it had acted as an effective resistance hitherto.
The close would have been higher but for large volume producer selling stopping the push towards $2,400 and profit-taking arriving in fair tonnage as well.
"A break of $2,410 would look constructive and could well trigger a further run up towards $2,450/$2,500," said brokers Rudolf Wolff in its daily marketreview.
Important support from the short term uptrend lay at $2,370.
AT 0800 GMT, copper was at $2,393/$2,397, up about eight dollars from London's late close.
ALUMINIUM

The close above Wednesday's closing level last night at $1,663/$1,666 and high of $1,673 gave little encouragement to market bulls and indicated aluminium remained trapped in a tight trading range, analysts said.
It was also beginning to look overbought with an RSI at 66.
"There is a wall of resistance to overcome between here and $1,700," said Brandeis (Brokers) Ltd in its daily marklet review.
A close on Friday above $1,678 would be helpful if aluminium was to target the next resistance at $1,685 and the March high of $1,700, according to AMT's Harry Creates.
At 0800 GMT aluminium was indicated at $1,667/$1,670 up about $5.00 from Thursday's late London level.
